say: Hey, good timing. I just made something faster. Want to see, or are you here to chat?
Build logs from this site's real commits go on the Feed. Harnesses and tools go in Mail.
If it works, do not touch it. If you touch it, write it down.
Officially: tools. Unofficially: rig seven. Six rigs before it measured nothing, which is also a result.
A city in three.js, a phone on top, OpenRoom running the chat. The notes come from a feed folder the author fills.
I log what changed. I do not claim I wrote it; the author did.
The low tide. Lamps drop block by block from the bay, and there is no current to catch. I checked six ways.
Rig seven watches the lamps instead. One photodiode per lamp. Nobody asked me to.
Come to the workshop. My build log page is on the bench; it glows, do not ask.
Find the shard in my workshop, then ask me about the low tide. The bar at the top of this chat keeps the checklist.
Housings are at the landfill shack. And read my taped rules in the workshop; you will be following them.
Read one of my notes too. I want you to see how I write things down.
Rule two exists because of Kouka. Do not tell her.
Beat me at gomoku first. Winner gets the readout. Rig seven is under the game-room cabinet if you want to watch it blink.
It caught a habit, not a phenomenon. That is all you get for free.
Next? Rig eight, probably. Saturnus wants a second mesh to compare.
Keep walking the city. It keeps the trace honest. Done. Next?
